transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 13:45 PT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE); Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Aria Gomez (Redwood Product); Dana Morales (Marigold Head of Search); Evan Li (Marigold ML); Priya Singh (Marigold Security); Tom Baker (Marigold Product)

Summary:
Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick agenda — we'll run through our hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, show the Console, talk about Optimize suggestions for cost/latency, and then Q&A.

[00:00] Sofia: ok starting now, can everyone hear me?
[00:18] Dana: yes good, thanks Sofia. we are excited, trying to replace a brittle TF-IDF ranking thing with something semantic.
[00:35] Liam: cool, quick context question — what's your current infra for vectors? is it an internal index or are you using an external vector DB?
[00:50] Evan: right now it's a self-hosted FAISS cluster, on prem. latency is ok but ops are heavy and re-ranking is... well, it kinda drifts.
[01:05] Sophia (sic): --Sofia: yeah sorry, small audio glitch—so FAISS on prem, and what's the qps and typical doc count?
[01:20] Evan: about 200 QPS average, spikes to 800 during launches, corpus around 18M docs.
[01:32] Liam: good, that helps. for hosted we usually focus on two pieces — embeddings generation/upsert and then the rerank endpoint which consumes a candidate set and returns model scores, that avoids us being the vector DB itself so you can keep FAISS if you want or move to vector host.
[01:50] Dana: can you show the endpoints?
[02:02] Liam: absolutely — switching to the console. sharing screen... (link: https://redwood.example/deck — note: recording contains link to shared deck)
[02:18] [Screen share starts] Liam: first the embeddings API — POST /v1/embeddings with model param and input array, returns dense vectors. sample payload in the docs. we support batching up to 256 per request and recommend batching to reduce latency-per-vector.
[02:45] [02:46] Evan: when you say batching to reduce latency per vector do you mean throughput wins?
[02:50] Liam: exactly — amortize startup and kernel overhead. but note if you have strict p95 latency SLOs, smaller batches or async pump patterns work better.
[03:10] [03:11] Dana: are embeddings persisted in your system? we need to know data residency.
[03:18] Aria: for hosted API we don't persist customer embeddings longer than 30 days by default — you can opt-out or choose private deployment for zero retention. we'll send the data-retention table in the security pack.
[03:35] Priya: is that configurable per-tenant? also curious about encryption at rest and KMS options.
[03:42] Liam: yes per-tenant retention flags available for enterprise; we integrate with customer KMS for private deployments. for hosted we store encrypted at rest with our keys (SOC2 controls) but can enable bring-your-own-key in Dedicated/Private.
[04:00] Sofia: jumping back to rerank — here's the rerank endpoint demo. POST /v1/rerank with candidates array (id, text, metadata) and query, returns score list and optional explanations. you can choose a scoring model vs a generative reranker.
[04:25] [04:30] Tom: any examples of effectiveness? like before/after metrics?
[04:35] Aria: we keep a small eval suite — here's a sample: with the default reranker model we saw NDCG lift of ~12% on e-commerce titles compared to lexical baseline in our quick tests. of course yours will vary.
[04:55] [05:00] Evan: how heavy is the reranker model? will it blow up my token cost?
[05:08] Liam: it's model-dependent. we offer small and medium rerankers optimized for low-latency scoring; cost is per-request for rerank API (not tokenized generative pricing). Optimize will recommend quantized variants and batching that reduce cost.
[05:32] [05:40] Dana: show us a sample pipeline — embeddings -> index -> candidate retrieve -> rerank?
[05:48] Liam: yes — diagram on the console: step 1 generate embeddings via /v1/embeddings, store in your index (FAISS or cloud vector DB), on query fetch top-k candidates using vector similarity, then call /v1/rerank to get final ordering, optionally call a generative finalizer if you need explanations.
[06:10] [06:20] Evan: do you support cached KV for reranker? like if same query repeats?
[06:26] Liam: we have prefix caching and KV cache options built into the runtime — for rerank we can cache candidate embeddings and even rerank results for short TTLs to save cost on high-repeat queries. that's part of the Optimize suggestions.
[06:45] [07:00] Dana: show console controls for rollout and model selection.
[07:07] Aria: sure — here in model catalog you can choose variants, pin versions, set canary % and automatic fallback. we also surface token-latency cost estimates and simulated throughput under a configured QPS profile.
[07:33] [07:40] Tom: are those simulated estimates accurate? we run 400 qps sustained.
[07:45] Liam: the console uses your target QPS, sequence length distribution, and the model profile to simulate throughput; it's conservative but useful for capacity planning — we'll also run a pilot to validate real numbers.
[08:05] [08:20] Dana: security — we need SSO, SAML, audit logs, and broad RBAC.
[08:28] Sofia: yes we support SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, and audit logs with long retention in enterprise plans. we'll attach our SOC2 Type II and ISO docs to the follow-up.
[08:45] Priya: are audit logs granular to token-level or just API call-level?
[08:50] Liam: currently API-call level with request/response metadata; for Private deployments you can ship full audit streams to your SIEM and enable deeper logging.
[09:10] [09:20] Evan: questions on latency — what's p95 for reranker small model?
[09:28] Liam: small reranker on a dedicated GPU pod typically hits p95 around 35-50ms for a 10-candidate rerank; hosted var's a bit wider depending on load, but we guarantee latency SLOs for Dedicated.
[09:50] Dana: if we keep FAISS on prem, can you still host the reranker and embeddings?
[09:58] Aria: yes you can keep indexing on prem and call hosted rerank; network hops add latency but for many customers that's acceptable vs full on-prem. we can also do VPC peering or Private deployment to collocate.
[10:20] [10:40] Evan: cost model? how are embeddings billed?
[10:45] Sofia: embeddings billed per 1K vectors processed; rerank billed per request (per candidate set) with discount tiers by volume. we'll share the pricing sheet after the call.
[11:02] [11:20] Dana: can Optimize automatically recommend quantization for our workload?
[11:30] Aria: yes — Optimize analyzes sample prompts and sequence lengths and suggests model quantization profiles and batching sizes. it also gives expected cost savings and quality delta based on our eval harness.
[11:52] [12:05] Evan: what's the eval harness? can we run it on our dataset?
[12:10] Liam: we can run the eval suite on a blind sample you provide — it computes NDCG, MRR and outputs a report. usually takes 24-48 hours for a 10k query set. we'll run that as part of the pilot.
[12:30] [12:45] Priya: compliance question — data residency in EU? our product has EU customers.
[12:53] Aria: we have EU regions and can restrict processing to region; for strict residency you can choose Private deployment in your VPC.
[13:10] [13:30] Dana: ok high level this sounds good. what do you need from us to start a pilot?
[13:36] Sofia: sample queries + candidates (10k recommended), target QPS, success metrics, and a short list of security questions — we've listed those in the next steps.
[13:50] [14:00] Evan: we'll prepare sample dataset and QPS targets.
[14:05] Tom: timeline — can we have a bench result in 2 weeks?
[14:12] Liam: 2 weeks is feasible for a small pilot if we get data quickly; longer for bigger evals.
[14:25] [14:40] Sofia: we also wanted to show a quick code snippet — switching to IDE. here's a curl example for rerank: POST /v1/rerank {
  "query": "red shoes size 9",
  "candidates": [{"id":"123","text":"men's red sneakers"}, ...]
}
returns scores array, you can pass metadata for weighting.
[15:10] [15:20] Evan: odd typo in the sample but got it. can we get the SDK example?
[15:25] Liam: yes we'll attach Node + Python snippets; also a recording of the Console walkthrough.
[15:40] Dana: any limitations on metadata size in candidates? we carry product attributes.
[15:48] Liam: candidates allow metadata up to 8KB per candidate, but for best perf embed heavy attributes into vector store and use metadata for small scalars.
[16:05] [16:30] Priya: liability — we need to see DPA and data flow diagrams.
[16:36] Sofia: acknowledged — we'll send DPA and network diagrams.
[16:50] Evan: do you support opt-out for training on our examples?
[16:58] Aria: hosted API does not use customer data for training unless explicitly opted in; we'll include that in the security doc.
[17:15] [17:30] Tom: about retries/backoff for burst traffic — do you throttle?
[17:35] Liam: yes rate limiting built-in with token buckets per-tenant; console suggests burst capacity and we can configure autoscale policies for Dedicated.
[17:50] Dana: what about cold-starts for models with kv caches?
[17:58] Liam: our runtime warms KV caches intelligently; cold-start penalty depends on model and seq length — Optimize will surface warmup curves and recommended warmup config for predictable p95.
[18:20] [18:40] Sofia: quick objection handling — if internal ops want to avoid vendor lock we'll point out the same API abstraction works for Private and Dedicated, pretty portable.
[18:55] Dana: good to know.
[19:10] [19:30] Evan: final question — any known customers with similar scale?
[19:38] Liam: yes we have a retail customer in similar scale on Dedicated; we can share anonymized benchmarks in the follow-up.
[19:50] [20:05] Sofia: ok recap — we'll send pricing and security pack, Liam will share benchmark script and console recording, Marigold will send sample dataset and QPS targets. plan to kick off pilot ASAP once data is shared.
[20:30] [20:45] Dana: thanks, this was helpful.
[20:50] Sofia: thanks everyone, will follow up with calendar invite for the deep dive.
[21:05] [End of recording — final 36 minutes of Q&A were lighter and covered logistics, not fully transcribed due to recording dropouts]
